text:
Brett Pesce has already passed last season's point total, and that says as much about last season as this one. He had 7 points in 37 games in 2025-26; he has 11 in 23 now, all but one of them assists, on more than 21 minutes a night for a Devils team that has won seven of its last ten games he's played.

The process backs him up. New Jersey wins 58.2% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five with Pesce on the ice, about three points better than without him, and the luck around him is close to neutral. His closest statistical match is Jonas Brodin, which tells you the style: penalty kill, 43 blocked shots, defense first.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a small sample, shows both edges: he stopped 22% of entries at his blue line (typical 11%) but kept possession on only 20% of his exits. His 1.35 points per 60 sit above our talent range, so the assists will slow. He missed time in mid-November before CBS Sports reported him "Back at practice" on Nov. 17. Healthy, he's the steady partner every good team needs.
headline: Pesce is quietly making it work
